entries.name: GeoLibre Desktop
description:
GeoLibre is a lightweight, cloud-native desktop GIS for visualizing and
      analyzing geospatial data, built on MapLibre with deck.gl for 3D and
      large point-cloud overlays.

It loads vector and raster files, web services, ArcGIS layers, MBTiles,
      3D Tiles, and cloud-native formats such as GeoParquet, FlatGeobuf,
      PMTiles, and COG, converting local data in the browser with DuckDB-WASM
      Spatial. Projects are saved in an open .geolibre.json format, and the app
      is extensible through a plugin ecosystem.
Highlights:
Add data from files, web services, databases, and cloud catalogs
Vector and raster processing tools, with an optional Python sidecar
A SQL workspace for DuckDB Spatial, and a docked Jupyter notebook
Offline basemap downloads, story maps, and multi-user collaboration
entries.summary: Lightweight, cloud-native GIS platform

entries.name: Talaria
description:
This is the official desktop client for Talaria. Talaria is one workspace
      where the whole day actually happens: chat, boards, docs, plans, research.
      Agents work in it as real teammates, in your channels and on your tickets.
      Humans approve.

Add a hosted or self-hosted instance by URL. Switch between them in a
      click. Each one keeps its own saved session.
Add hosted or self-hosted instances by URL
Switch workspaces in a click
Each instance keeps its own saved session
entries.summary: Official desktop client for the workspace where agents work as teammates

entries.name: ZenNotes
description:
ZenNotes is a keyboard-first Markdown notes app that keeps your notes as
      ordinary Markdown files on disk — yours to own, sync, and version however
      you like.
On top of the files you already own, it adds:
Vim-friendly editing with split and live-preview workflows
Wiki-links, tags, tasks, daily notes, and full-text search
Diagrams (Mermaid, TikZ), math (KaTeX), and syntax-highlighted code
CSV databases with Notion-style Table and Board views over plain .csv files
Archive, trash, quick capture, and a built-in command-line companion
entries.summary: Keyboard-first Markdown notes app

entries.name: Annotator
description:
Elementary-style image annotation and editing: add arrows, text,
      shapes, blur, highlights and numbering to screenshots, then crop,
      scale or export the result. Built around the idea that pointing at
      the thing beats describing the thing.
entries.summary: Communicate with images better

entries.name: AI Gate
description:
AI Gate brings all major AI assistants — ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, Qwen, and Grok —
      into one beautiful, unified desktop application. No more switching between browser tabs.
Key features:
Multi-panel workspace: view up to 3 AI tools side-by-side simultaneously
Global webview pool: switching layouts preserves all session state — no reloads, no flashing
Smart tab synchronization: synced or independent tabs per panel
Native Wayland support with automatic X11/Wayland detection
System tray integration: minimize to tray and restore instantly
Auto-updates via GitHub releases
Privacy first: no telemetry, no trackers
entries.summary: Access all your AI tools seamlessly in one unified desktop application

entries.name: Gale
description:
A lightweight and user-friendly app for installing and managing mods on the Thunderstore
            platform.

Gale supports every game and mod loader found on thunderstore.io, including Lethal
            Company, R.E.P.O., Hollow Knight Silksong and over 100 others.
entries.summary: Modern mod manager for Thunderstore

entries.name: Macro Trainer
description:
Macro Trainer is a privacy-first macro tracking application. Track your
      daily nutrition and calories locally on your device — no subscriptions,
      no cloud syncing, no ads. The Linux build is free.
Features:
Log meals against a large built-in food database, entirely offline
Daily macro and calorie dashboard
AI coaching that adjusts your plan as you go
Intermittent fasting timer
Body weight and progress tracking charts
Your data stays on your device
entries.summary: Privacy-first macro tracking

entries.name: Redis Viewer
description:
Redis Viewer is a local Redis desktop client for browsing large keyspaces,
      inspecting Java serialized values, and analyzing SlowLog, BigKey, HotKey,
      CPU, memory, and cache-hit signals.
Browse large keyspaces with SCAN and virtual scrolling
Inspect Java serialized, Base64, Hex, and binary values
Analyze SlowLog, BigKey, HotKey, and resource trends
Store connection passwords in the system keychain
entries.summary: Redis desktop client for large keyspaces and bottleneck analysis

entries.name: OpenHome
description:
OpenHome is an open source tool for moving Pokémon between game save files, including
      forwards and backwards through generations, without data loss.

The Flatpak version may run into extra issues due to the nature
      of Flatpak sandboxing. When submitting bugs, please specify you are using the Flatpak version.
entries.summary: An open source tool for moving Pokémon between game save files

entries.name: NovaCut
description:
NovaCut is a video editor for Linux desktops: the fast, touch-friendly
      workflow of a mobile editor, with a real multi-track timeline underneath.
      It runs natively on Wayland and keeps the preview live while you cut.
What it does:
Magnetic timeline with separate lanes for main video, overlays, text, adjustment layers and audio
Trim handles, razor cut (S or Ctrl+B), snapping (N) and timeline zoom
Live preview canvas with 16:9, 9:16, 1:1 and 4:5 project presets
Text and typography layers with fonts, colours, outlines and shadows
Speed ramping, audio waveforms, and a canvas-based smart cutout that needs no model or network access
50 transitions and 50 effects, including cinema LUTs
A plugin marketplace with declarative manifest.json filters, four presets included (Cyberpunk Neon, 80s Retro VHS, Cinematic Golden Hour, Film Noir) and an in-app filter creator
Hardware-accelerated decode for preview (VA-API)

Probing, preview and export use the ffmpeg and ffprobe that ship with the
      freedesktop runtime, and the export dialog offers what that build
      supports. Speech-to-text captions are not available in this package: they
      need a whisper.cpp build and a Whisper model, and neither is in the
      project repository yet.

Projects, downloaded plugins and fonts are kept in the application's own
      data directory. The app reaches the network only for marketplace plugins
      and stock media the user asks for, and it sends no telemetry.
entries.summary: CapCut-style video editor with a multi-track timeline and plugin marketplace

entries.name: OmaAmp
description:
OmaAmp is a Winamp 2.91-style audio player for Linux, written in Python with
      Qt. It plays local files with a real DSP chain behind it — a 10-band IIR
      biquad equalizer, a preamp with a soft limiter, and an FFT spectrum analyzer
      driven by the audio actually playing rather than by a decoration.
What it does:
The classic modular layout: main window with LED clock, spectrum analyzer, marquee, specs readout, volume, balance and seek
10-band graphic equalizer (60 Hz to 16 kHz) with presets, preamp and a live frequency-response curve
Six visualizer modes — spectrum analyzer, laser oscilloscope, dual VU meters, warp starfield, matrix rain and a polar frequency ring
Playlist editor with drag and drop, search, M3U/PLS import and export, and state restored on restart
Theme engine with bundled themes, an in-app theme studio, and .wsz skin support
Internet radio from a searchable directory and direct stream URLs, plus YouTube audio streams
MP3, FLAC, WAV, OGG and AAC playback
English and Swedish interface

Playing local files needs no network at all. Radio, YouTube streams and the
      optional theme-sharing feature do, and they are the only things that use it: the
      radio directory (radio-browser.info), whatever stream URL you paste, and — only if
      you paste a GitHub token of your own — the GitHub API, to publish a shared theme as
      a gist in your account. There is no telemetry, no account of the app's own, and no
      background update check.
entries.summary: Winamp-style audio player with themes, equalizer and visualizers

entries.name: OmarchyTube
description:
OmarchyTube is a standalone YouTube window for Omarchy and Hyprland — the
      ReVanced/SmartTube idea without a browser around it. It opens full-screen and
      stays out of the way, so the video gets the whole display instead of a tab.
What it does:
TV (leanback) mode for arrow-key and remote navigation, and a desktop mode you toggle with F2
Sign-in through Google's OAuth device flow: a QR code is shown and the session is stored locally — no password is typed into the app
Ad blocking at the request level, plus cosmetic filtering of sponsored shelves and banners, and skipping of pre-roll and mid-roll ads
SponsorBlock segment skipping, with the segments marked on the progress bar and an on-screen "unskip" button
Return YouTube Dislike counts on the player
Hardware-accelerated video decode (VA-API)
Its own browsing grid as the start screen — seven columns of cards at 1920x1080 where the leanback view shows one row of four — with search and arrow-key navigation

The app talks to three services and no others: YouTube, the SponsorBlock API and
      the Return YouTube Dislike API. It sends no telemetry and has no analytics. It is an
      independent client and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or built by YouTube.
entries.summary: Full-screen YouTube client with ad blocking and SponsorBlock

entries.name: OmaScribe
description:
OmaScribe is a word processor for Linux that writes like a document editor and
      reads like a writing tool: rich text with styles, tables, images and charts, a
      vault of templates, and an AI review that works on the text you have selected
      rather than on the whole document.
What it does:
Rich text editing with styles, tables, charts, images and print layout
DOCX, PDF, Markdown, plain text and HTML import and export
AI review and inline suggestions through any OpenAI-compatible endpoint the user configures
A vault of templates and reusable documents, plus a research panel
Document statistics, a code analyser and a ghostwriter mode
Google Fonts browser with download into the document
Swedish and English interface
Dictation, when the optional faster-whisper dependency is available

The AI features only ever talk to the endpoint you configure yourself — there is
      no built-in service, no account, and no telemetry. Local models work too: point it
      at a llama.cpp, vLLM or Ollama-compatible URL on your own machine.
entries.summary: Rich text editor with AI review, vault and document export

entries.name: Sonix Studio
description:
Sonix Studio is a digital audio workstation for Linux, written in Rust with an
      egui interface. It edits audio directly on the timeline, the way FL Studio does,
      with magnetic loop snapping — and keeps the engine's word: everything the
      interface advertises is wired to real DSP, including the parts that are still
      rough.
Features include:
Timeline arranger with direct clip editing, slicing and magnetic loop snapping
Real-time cpal/ALSA audio engine, with the system's PipeWire working through its ALSA layer
16-step channel rack, piano roll, and touch instruments
Analog Alchemy synthesizer, drum synthesis, per-voice filter and envelope
Multichannel effects mixer with per-track sends, automation lanes and VCA groups
Vocal Studio with microphone recording, a sampler and a pitch-preserving time-stretch
Stem separation (DSP path), a stem focus editor and Suno stem-pack import
Plugin host: catalogues everything, and loads CLAP, VST3 and VST2 effects with delay compensation
Optional AI music assistant speaking to any OpenAI-compatible endpoint
Export to WAV/MP3/FLAC with the master mix or per-track stems

Two things are deliberately opt-in rather than shipped: neural stem separation
      (needs a build with the neural feature plus a user-supplied HTDemucs model — the
      DSP separator is what runs without one) and LV2 plugin loading, which has no host
      yet. The project says so itself in its README rather than in a footnote.
entries.summary: Native Linux digital audio workstation

entries.name: MA-TUI
description:
MA-TUI is a terminal interface for Music Assistant: browse your library and
      providers, control playback, volume, grouping and queues across your
      networked speakers, and follow podcasts and audiobooks with resume points
      and played-episode tracking. It also registers the machine it runs on as a
      Sendspin speaker, so Music Assistant can send audio there directly, without
      a separate companion player process.
entries.summary: Terminal controller and local speaker for Music Assistant

entries.name: Jots
description:
Jots is a fast, lightweight sticky-notes app: Markdown editing with
      live formatting and checklists, plain .md file storage you can back
      up anywhere, and 12 pastel themes that hold up in light and dark
      mode.

Notes can sync to any Git remote on a schedule or on demand, a
      privacy mode hides sensitive text on screen, and an MCP server lets
      compatible AI assistants create, search and manage notes directly.
entries.summary: Lightweight sticky notes for Linux with Markdown and AI-ready sync

entries.name: Tabularis
description:
Tabularis is a modern, cross-platform database manager designed for developers.
      It supports MySQL, PostgreSQL, and SQLite with an intuitive interface for browsing
      tables, running queries, and managing database connections.
entries.summary: A database manager for developers

entries.name: Luma
description:
Luma plays many audio tracks at once and lets you control each one
      independently, with the look and feel of a professional studio
      tool. A focused native app for sound technicians and broadcast
      operators.
entries.summary: Real-time multitrack audio mixer for Linux

entries.name: Edconv
description: A user-friendly interface that simplifies the power of FFmpeg. It's designed for fast and efficient conversion of video and audio files.
entries.summary: An intuitive FFmpeg GUI

entries.name: Zephyr
description: Zephyr is a state-of-the-art cross-platform GUI client for Mihomo, combining modern desktop aesthetics, high performance with Rust and Tauri v2, and a 13-layer security defense architecture.
High performance and low memory footprint with Tauri v2 and native Rust IPC
Zero heavyweight frontend frameworks — pure native JavaScript UI
Full proxy protocol management, subscription parsing, and latency testing
Real-time traffic oscilloscope monitoring and system tray integration
entries.summary: A modern, lightweight Mihomo GUI client

entries.name: Vish
description:
Vish is an editor for creating Bash scripts using a node interface. 
        It allows users to design their scripts by connecting nodes that represent different 
        Bash commands and basic programming concepts.
        Vish is made for educational purposes and to simplify the process of creating Bash scripts.
entries.summary: Visual Bash Editor

entries.name: Rocker
description:
Rocker is a native desktop client for Docker containers, written in
      pure Rust on egui: no webview, no bundled Chromium, no Electron.
      Browse images, inspect and manage containers, and follow logs from
      a lightweight native UI.
entries.summary: Native desktop client for Docker containers

entries.name: File Crate
description:
File Crate is a native archive viewer, extractor and creator built
      for the COSMIC desktop. It opens ZIP, 7Z, RAR, TAR, TAR.GZ, TAR.XZ
      and TAR.ZST archives, and creates ZIP, 7Z and TAR-family archives
      with password protection for ZIP.
entries.summary: Your archives, neatly packed

entries.name: SaveState
description: A versatile game save backup manager, featuring Steam detection, Minecraft support, drag & drop, desktop shortcuts and emulator compatible.
entries.summary: A simple game save manager

entries.name: Kai
description:
Kai is a versatile AI assistant that connects to multiple AI services including
      Ollama, Google Gemini, OpenAI ChatGPT, Anthropic Claude, Mistral, Groq,
      OpenRouter, and any OpenAI-compatible API.
Features:
Chat with multiple AI providers from a single app
Run local AI models via Ollama
Text-to-speech support
Image attachments and analysis
Customizable system prompts
Multiple conversation management
Available on Android, iOS, Desktop, and Web
entries.summary: AI assistant powered by Ollama, Gemini, ChatGPT and more

entries.name: ClamAV-GUI
description:
ClamAV-GUI wraps the ClamAV antivirus engine in a Qt interface:
      on-demand and scheduled scans, signature updates through freshclam,
      and clamd configuration, without touching the command line.

Scans can be launched from the window or by dropping files onto the
      drop zone; results, quarantine handling and scan logs are presented
      per profile. The UI ships German natively and carries community
      translations that the author asks native speakers to review.
entries.summary: Qt front-end for the ClamAV antivirus engine

entries.name: IPFS Desktop
description:
IPFS Desktop gives you all the power of IPFS in a convenient desktop app:
      a complete IPFS node, plus handy OS menubar/taskbar shortcuts and an all-in-one
      file manager, peer map, and content explorer.

Use IPFS Desktop to get acquainted with IPFS without needing to touch the
      terminal — or, if you're already experienced, use the powerful menubar/taskbar
      shortcuts alongside the command line to make your IPFS workflow faster.
Features include:
Start your node at system startup and control it from your OS system tray
Quickly import files, folders, and screenshots to IPFS
Easily manage the contents of your node (pin, preview, rename, and share)
Visualize your IPFS peers worldwide on an interactive world map
Explore the "Merkle Forest" of IPFS files and content-addressed data
OS-wide protocol handler support for ipfs:// and ipns:// links
entries.summary: An unobtrusive and user-friendly desktop application for IPFS

entries.name: Graphics Creator
description:
Graphics Creator is a Qt-based tool for building animated titles and
      visual effects on a keyframe timeline: strokes, color and font
      mixing, long shadows, waves, text animators and easing curves.

Projects render to animated graphics suitable for video overlays and
      titles. Works alongside the author's other creative tools and ships
      an AUR package for Arch users.
entries.summary: Create titles and visual effects with keyframes

entries.name: Discord Chat Exporter
description: Features:
Export to HTML, plain text, CSV, or JSON
Filter by date range
Support for attachments, embeds, and reactions
Dark and light HTML themes
Works with user tokens and bot tokens
entries.summary: Export Discord chat logs to a file

entries.name: Anvil Organizer
description:
Anvil Organizer is a native Linux mod manager for games like Skyrim,
      Fallout 4, Cyberpunk 2077, Baldur's Gate 3, Starfield, and more.

Inspired by Mod Organizer 2, it features virtual file system deployment,
      profile management, Nexus Mods integration, drag-and-drop load ordering,
      and plugin conflict detection.
entries.summary: Native Linux Mod Manager inspired by Mod Organizer 2

entries.name: MCCompanion
description:
MCCompanion lets you connect to external Minecraft servers from
      PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo Switch and other consoles, bridging
      any server to your local network so consoles can join as if it
      were a LAN game.

It also packs tools for skins, player lookup, server tracking and
      a built-in wiki.
entries.summary: The Minecraft companion app

entries.name: Keyoxide
description:
Keyoxide allows you to prove “ownership” of accounts on websites, domain
      names, IM, etc., regardless of your username.

When you visit someone’s Keyoxide profile and see a green tick next to an
      account on some website, it was proven beyond doubt that the same person
      who set up this profile also holds that account.
App features:
Runs on Linux desktop and mobile
Simple and straightforward UI
Onboarding and guided tour
Fully open source
Supports fingerprint and email address as identifiers
Supports fetching identities via keyservers and Web Key Directory
Deep linking with openpgp4fpr and aspe URL schemes
Search history
Contacts feature
ASP profile management: create, edit, delete, import, export profiles and add claims directly within the app
Hide sensitive user profiles and protect them with authentication
Add multiple PGP or ASP profiles
Available in 11 languages
entries.summary: Verify decentralized cryptographic identities on the go

entries.name: LibreDB Studio
description:
LibreDB Studio is an open-source SQL IDE for developers and data teams. The desktop
      app runs entirely on your machine: it starts a local LibreDB Studio server in the
      background and shows it in a native window. Nothing is sent to a cloud service.
Databases it speaks:
PostgreSQL
MySQL and MariaDB
SQLite
Microsoft SQL Server
Oracle Database
MongoDB
Redis
What you get:
A Monaco-based SQL editor with schema-aware completion and formatting
A virtualized results grid built for large result sets, with CSV and JSON export
Schema browser, entity-relationship diagrams and index advice
Query plans, slow-query and session monitoring
Optional AI assistance (natural language to SQL, query explanation) using your own API key
An embedded sample database, so there is something to query on first launch

Connections are made over TCP. The sandbox has no access to your home directory by
      default; grant it explicitly if you need to open SQLite files or reach a database
      through a Unix socket - the project documentation lists the exact commands.
entries.summary: AI-powered SQL IDE for PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB and more

entries.name: Letter Friends
description:
Letter Friends is a keyboard for children too young to read: keys
      speak their letters and sounds, helping pre-literate kids to
      explore typing and words on their own.
entries.summary: A keyboard for children too young to read

entries.name: OpenRGB E1.31 Receiver Plugin
description:
This OpenRGB plugin adds E1.31 integration, the industry-standard
      lighting protocol supported by a wide variety of control software
      and often used for sequenced light shows. Control all of your
      OpenRGB-supported hardware from these programs by turning your
      setup into an E1.31 receiver.
entries.summary: Turn your OpenRGB setup into an E1.31 receiver

entries.name: OpenRGB Effects Plugin
description:
Synchronize your OpenRGB lighting with a wide variety of
      customizable effects including audio visualizations, screen
      mirroring (Ambilight), OpenGL shaders, and many more.
entries.summary: Synchronize OpenRGB lighting with customizable effects

entries.name: OpenRGB Visual Map Plugin
description:
This OpenRGB plugin lets you organize your real devices on a map
      and create one or many virtual devices. Apply gradients (presets
      or custom) across the layout and expose it to other plugins such
      as the Effects engine.
entries.summary: Map real devices and create virtual ones in OpenRGB

entries.name: Tahoma2D
entries.description: Continuity submission. Tahoma2D (657 stars) had its Flathub submission (flathub/flathub#8742) denied over a filesystem=home lint exception — without it the app "cannot save anything and is rendered completely useless", as the author put it — and he closed it himself. omapak picked it up. Manifest from that PR unchanged; shared-modules vendored.
entries.summary: Tahoma2D, a 2D animation and compositing application for making short films and illustrations
